## #2 — podperson — 2013-10-04
<https://www.cheetah3d.com/forum/index.php?threads/9882/post-82128>

Did you see the other thread on learning to script? I posted the relevant chapter of my book in it.

Swizl linked this interactive Javascript tutorial in another thread:

http://www.codecademy.com/#!/exercises/0

Perhaps even more useful, here's the Khan Academy's CS course (which is Javascript):

http://www.khanacademy.org/cs/programming

Advanced Javascript:

http://ejohn.org/apps/learn/

As for documentation: on my site I provide this script -- Object Info -- which will produce markdown-formatted information about a selected object. If you install Mou (or a similar program) then it will cause beautiful documentation to appear for any object you select.

I've been programming for so long it's hard for me to think back on how one first learns to program. HTML and CSS are declarative languages (you describe objects), whereas Javascript is an imperative language (you tell the computer what to do) which is very different. Every statement in a javascript program (usually a statement is a line of code) is an instruction to do something, e.g. create a variable named a (var a, set a to be "hello world", (a = "hello world" and so on.

Programming is mostly breaking something you want the computer to do down into steps simple enough for the computer to do that thing. The hard part is breaking the task down, recognizing the kinds of steps the computer can do, and then seeing the pitfalls the computer could run into in following your instructions.

Links: http://ejohn.org/apps/learn/, http://loewald.com/c3dbook/Scripts/Object-Info/, http://www.codecademy.com/#%21/exercises/0, http://www.khanacademy.org/cs/programming, https://www.dropbox.com/s/czssk8t43naclul/Learn%203D%20with%20Cheetah%203D%20v6%20%E2%80%94%20Scripts.pdf
